title: Flourless walnut cake
subtitle: a dense, naturally gluten-free cake made entirely from blitzed walnuts and eggs
excerpt: Flourless walnut cake is made from walnuts blitzed to a coarse meal, beaten with eggs and sugar, and baked to a dense, sticky crumb with a strong walnut flavour. It contains no flour of any kind and is naturally gluten-free. The cake is best left for a day before serving; the flavour deepens and the texture becomes fudgier as it settles.
sourceNotes: Flourless nut cakes are common throughout the Mediterranean and central Europe, where ground or blitzed nuts substituted for flour in areas where wheat was scarce. Walnut cakes of this style are documented in Turkish, Greek, and Balkan cookbooks.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze whole, well wrapped, for up to 2 months. Defrost at room temperature overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4 to 5 days. The texture improves overnight.

content.text: Flourless walnut cake is made entirely from blitzed walnuts and eggs, with no flour or butter. The food processor does most of the work: the walnuts go in whole and come out as a coarse meal that gives the cake its dense, slightly sticky character. The walnut flavour is strong and direct.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease a 20 cm round cake tin and line the base with baking paper.
Blitz the walnuts in a food processor until they form a coarse meal. Do not over-process; the meal should have some texture, not be as fine as flour. Transfer to a bowl.
Beat the egg yolks with 150 g of the caster sugar until pale and thick, about 3 minutes. Stir in the vanilla, cinnamon, and baking powder. Fold in the walnut meal.

In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites to stiff peak. Add the remaining 50 g sugar and beat briefly until glossy. Fold one third of the whites into the walnut mixture to loosen it, then fold in the remaining whites in two additions.
Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until set and a skewer comes out clean. Leave to cool completely in the tin before removing.

attrs.problem: Cake dry and crumbly rather than dense and fudgy
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-blitzing the walnuts to a fine powder; too-fine walnut meal absorbs moisture and produces a dryer result.
attrs.fix: Blitz in short pulses and stop when the walnuts look like rough breadcrumbs with visible pieces still in the mix.

attrs.problem: Egg whites deflating when folded in
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-mixing when folding; each fold collapses a little of the air beaten into the whites.
attrs.fix: Use a large spatula and a gentle cutting-and-lifting motion. Stop as soon as the whites are just incorporated, even if a few small white streaks remain.
